prompt: Create a single original portrait of the unnamed armed traveller who first appears beside the Prior in Walter Scott's Ivanhoe chapter II paragraphs 6–8 (later called Brian de Bois-Guilbert). He is a muscular, lean man a little past forty, tall and hardened by travel, with strongly sun-browned skin, powerful angular features, thick black moustaches, piercing dark eyes, a deep healed scar across the brow and a very subtle unevenness of one eyelid, NOT blindness or an eye patch. A close scarlet cap edged with fur, rounded and flat like a shallow inverted mortar, covers his head; no tassel, crown or tall bishop's hat. He wears a long scarlet monastic mantle with a simple white cloth cross on the RIGHT shoulder over a flexible linked-mail shirt, sleeves and mail gloves. A long straight double-edged dagger is sheathed at his belt; do not add a sword in his hand or fantasy plate armour. Upright three-quarter waist portrait on a wooded English travelling road at dusk, controlled impatient expression, no other people or identifiable future locations. Mature historical literary book-plate illustration, fine painterly oil and watercolour textures, realistic individual face, restrained crimson, iron grey and forest green, strong card-size silhouette. This is his first travelling costume, not the later purple silk and white banquet mantle. No prisoner, romance, flames, tournament defeat, supernatural light, exaggerated ethnic features, film-actor resemblance, text, logo or watermark.
review: Scarlet fur-edged cap, brow scar, dark moustaches, sun-browned face, linked mail gloves and long sheathed dagger are suitable. Rejected for white cross on the wearer's left shoulder (viewer-right); source expressly puts it on his right shoulder. Move the cross without mirroring the portrait.
